groups.note: The actual dative generation noun is the people toward whom the grieving/displeasure is directed; English with marks that governed participant relation without an independently printed Greek with preposition.

Pinned N1904 ταύτῃ is this generation; LSV that follows the distal demonstrative wording. The same historical generation is identified, with the proximal/distal difference explicit rather than a different participant.

The actual dative article/heart phrase marks the sphere of the wandering; English in their heart makes the same people’s body-part possessor explicit. The bracketed possessive belongs to this contextual case-marked phrase, not a separately written Greek their pronoun.

3:11.sourceText: ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου.
3:11.targetText: so I swore in My anger, They will [not] enter into My rest.”

groups.note: The εἰ plus entry predicate is the negative Semitic oath formula, literally if they will enter with an implied adverse oath consequence. LSV makes its denial explicit as They will not enter. The full oath constituent supports bracketed not; this is not a standalone lexical rule equating εἰ with not.

3:12.sourceText: βλέπετε, ἀδελφοί, μή ποτε ἔσται ἔν τινι ὑμῶν καρδία πονηρὰ ἀπιστίας ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ζῶντος,

3:13.sourceText: ἀλλὰ παρακαλεῖτε ἑαυτοὺς καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν, ἄχρις οὗ τὸ Σήμερον καλεῖται, ἵνα μὴ σκληρυνθῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας·
3:13.targetText: but exhort one another every day, while [it] is called “Today,” that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin,

groups.note: The actual reflexive yourselves is used reciprocally of the community exhorting its members; LSV renders one another, retaining those same recipients without substituting a different Greek reciprocal form.
The distributive κατά with each gives the every-day expression; both actual distributive components share English every.
Greek ἄχρις οὗ marks the temporal limit, as long as/until the time when; LSV while preserves that bounded temporal relation without a separate English word for each Greek component.
The negative μή with indefinite anyone, τις, jointly gives English none; the hardened predicate retains its own separate may-be-hardened realization.
Actual genitive article and sin noun jointly supply of ... sin as the deceitfulness qualifier. No independent Greek of preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article nominalizes the quoted Today time-label; English directly quotes Today without a definite article at the label.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an impersonal subject it in is called Today; no separately written Greek it pronoun occurs at this naming expression.

The actual genitive article qualifies confidence within beginning-of-the-confidence; LSV places confidence as the main English object. Its definite article retains the same confidence referent under that noun-phrase recast.
The actual ὑπόστασις noun is confidence/assurance here, a contextual sense distinct from subsistence in1:3; the exact source head remains preserved.

The actual firm predicate adjective qualifies the held beginning/initial confidence alongside the holding-fast verb. English condenses this firm-holding construction into we may hold fast; no actual firmness word is discarded.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the past-possession relative we had in recasting initial confidence as confidence at the beginning; Greek has no separately written we/had predicate in that nominal phrase.
